collections.title: Temples across India
collections.standfirst: Five routes that lead to temples, from Hampi and Thanjavur in the south to Konark and Khajuraho further north.
intro: These routes each end at, or pass through, a temple that is part of how the place is understood today. Some have ordered stops with a written story at each; others carry the route line and facts so far, with stories still to be written.
Pick the one nearest you, or treat the five as a way to compare how different regions built and used their temples.

collections.title: Royal cities of the south
collections.standfirst: Hampi, Thanjavur, Mahabalipuram and Mysore: four places where rulers and builders left a mark on the landscape.
intro: Each of these routes is a walk through a place with a royal past. Hampi and Thanjavur have the fullest stories on Naarad so far; Mysore and Mahabalipuram are listed with their route facts.

collections.title: Walks around Chennai
collections.standfirst: Eight recorded walks and hikes across Chennai: the Marina, the lighthouse, Velachery, Thiruvanmiyur, IIT Madras and more.
intro: These are recorded tracks around the city, so they show where people have actually walked rather than a planned itinerary. Distances and times are listed where they were measured.
Stops and stories for these routes are still being written.

collections.title: Cities of the north
collections.standfirst: Jaipur by bicycle, the lakes of Udaipur and the ghats of Varanasi at dawn.
intro: Three routes through northern cities, each suited to a different way of moving: cycling in Jaipur, a circuit in Udaipur, a walk at first light in Varanasi.

collections.title: Open-air routes
collections.standfirst: Coorg's plantations, the IIT Madras campus, a hidden lake near the Chennai airport and Auroville.
intro: Routes where the place is mostly green and open: plantations, a campus, a lake and a township. Wear shoes for uneven ground and carry water.
